designStatus: Original untested task design; no learner observations

tasks: In an actual locally appropriate modified game, contribute/listen/share work, agree and review fair rules, respond appropriately to another player, care for equipment and identify/report unsafe touching. Transfer to a different game. Broad goal review is not a sum of component-code labels.

Use a genuinely interdependent small-team task with room for different ideas and roles; contribute an idea, build on another idea and complete a fair share. A solo success or merely staying on the team is insufficient.

Agree initial game norms, play, identify a concrete fairness/safety issue and use the agreed process to review a rule. Retain the whole IiW school/community rule-maker cases and actual participation, plus rkr reasons/independent following. Local institutional examples are bound at use, not relabelled Australian political knowledge.

Use non-graphic supplied game scenarios to distinguish another person’s feelings from one’s own and choose helpful responses to physical injury, emotional stress and feeling unwell. In genuine safe opportunities, offer comfort/practical help without being prompted and seek appropriate adult support; never stage an injury or require touching/first-aid treatment. Retain the whole kindness and perspective cards and their vocabulary support as separate canonical checks. Do not infer private emotions from obedience or require positive feelings.

Use a complete craft making task to construct a suitable simple target/marker, retaining accurate cutting/folding/join selection/safety/storage. Then actually inspect, use, care for and restore the declared game material, play space and facilities: check for damage, store equipment appropriately, leave the space ready for another group and report an unsafe item to an appropriate adult rather than undertake repairs. Include a changed facility case, not only the craft kit. Complete fair group-work tasks separately; naming a rule does not establish actual care.

In the game context distinguish appropriate explained care from touching that is not OK and demonstrate telling an appropriate adult, including continuing to tell if needed. Preserve all body-ownership and protective-response checks; no injury/abuse simulation or learner-state inference.

Explain and play a selected familiar local game, communicating its purpose, rules, positions/basic actions and one’s own thinking/feelings. Change a condition and explain the consequence. This is a source-fit task, not a claim of knowledge of all sports.

Give another child enough clear instructions to play a selected familiar local game: purpose, space, roles/positions, allowed basic moves and ending/scoring conditions. The listener tries it, asks a clarification and the speaker revises an unclear instruction. Retain the full receiving-four-steps and changed drawing-instruction checks of r-Bg and explain why actual rules support fairness/safety. Game-specific content is supplied/learned material, not an invented universal sport inventory.

Choose a realistic personally relevant movement-learning target and timeframe, plan practice, record attempts/progress and review/adjust the approach. Targets are appropriate to the declared task/resources, not imported metre/height examples or body norms. Actual improvement is not guaranteed or required as proof of honest goal-setting. Retain whole cJ planning/monitoring/adjustment and v5 process reflection; this is a future evidence protocol, not fabricated observations. Inherited hard paths through task steps, growth mindset and learning from mistakes remain exact. Their broader canonical evidence is separately accounted for: choose an appropriate challenging multi-step task, recognise and acknowledge steps/progress, explain practice/strategy-related learning and use a genuine available past mistake/learning example. Do not create a mistake, frustration or a personal improvement history to make the evidence appear. Lack of such a child observation in this authoring review is not a coverage gap or a learner result.

At a natural pause in the game, describe a genuine feeling and the reason for a chosen action, then after the game compare the intended plan with what happened and identify a useful change. Retain whole emotional-expression and learning-reflection checks in an appropriate task language. No confusion, frustration or positive feeling is manufactured; none can be stated accurately where applicable. The during-play thinking component is checked directly rather than inferred solely from an after-game summary. Keep the whole kvr disagreement/choosing-to-tell/difficult-situation evidence separate from the source during-game feeling report; use genuine opportunities or declared scenario rehearsal as appropriate, without asserting an independent real event occurred. Reflection also requires a concrete process difference and a justified next change, not merely whether the game was liked.
